S-001-US1._title: A patient signs in with a phone number and a code
S-001-US1.description_md: A patient opens the BrightSmile website on their phone, enters their mobile number and receives a 6-digit code by SMS. Entering the code signs them in. A phone number the system has not seen before becomes a new account once the code is verified and the patient has typed their name. Wrong or expired codes are explained plainly and a new code can be asked for. After 5 wrong tries the patient must wait 15 minutes. The patient stays signed in for 7 days from their last use so they do not need a new SMS every visit. Why this priority: without patient sign-in no patient can book, which is the main goal of the product (booking online instead of by phone). It is also the only part of the system that costs money per use (SMS), so its limits matter from day one. Independent test: with a fake SMS sender, request a code for a phone number, read it from the fake sender, verify it, and see a signed-in session; repeat with a wrong code 5 times and see the 15-minute wait. Fully testable without any booking feature.

Given a code was sent, When the patient enters a wrong code, Then the system says the code is wrong, says how many tries are left, and offers to send a new code
Given a code was sent more than 10 minutes ago, When the patient enters it, Then the system says the code has expired and offers a new code

Given a signed-in patient who last used the site 6 days ago, When they open the site, Then they are still signed in
Given a signed-in patient who last used the site more than 7 days ago, When they open the site, Then they must sign in again
